newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks rebound, bonds little changed.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks rebound, bonds little changed.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose sharply in a late rebound Tuesday, while the dollar rose to its strongest level in 33 months against the German mark on talk that Germany's economic woes were deepening.
Bonds were little changed as investors digested the first leg of the Treasury's quarterly auctions to raise funds for government operations.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 51.57 points at 6,858.11, reversing the previous session's loss of 49 points. The Nasdaq Composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, was off 3.83 points at 1,331.51.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,302 to 1,186 on active volume of 480 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The late rally saw mutual fund traders flock to many of the big-name stocks that have driven the market higher in recent months. Oil shares in particular found support after a weak performance on Monday.
Chevron Corp., Exxon Corp. and Texaco Inc. were all among the Dow's strongest performers.
But the market's real test of confidence took place among technology stocks, which suffered a second straight session of stiff selling pressure.
Late in the day, however, some top names in the sector, notably Intel Corp., finally attracted buyers and traders said the buying interest seemed to spark a rapid-fire turnaround for big-name stocks.
"A lot of people were watching Intel today," said Mike Rothberg, director of portfolio trading at Cantor Fitzgerald.
Intel, the world's largest maker of computer chips is considered a technology bellwether and many analysts use the stock to gauge investor sentiment towards the sector.
In the bond market, the bellwether 30-year Treasury bond edged down 1/32, or 31 cents on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.71 percent from at 6.70 percent at Monday's close.
The dollar made a late push above 1.68 marks for the first time since May 1994 to fetch 1.6784 marks in late trading vs. 1.6562 late Monday. It rose to 123.42 Japanese yen from 122.77 yen.
Wheat prices soared due to serious shipping delays at Canadian grain ports that could lure foreign buyers to the United States.

About 1.5 million metric tons of Canadian wheat exports have been delayed since January due to severe winter weather, and the delays may back up February and March shipments as well. The weather slowed railroads from delivering Canadian wheat to western ports.
At the Chicago Board of Trade wheat for March delivery closed up 9-1/2 cents at $3.62 per bushel.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 finished 3.4 points lower at 4,304.3. The Tokyo stock market was closed for the National Foundation day holiday.
